persons.name: Warren Pixby
persons.note: THE 1835 POLL LIST ALONE. Read from poll_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G2a), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. poll_1835 names this person at Chicago by 31 December 1835 and nothing says when they came. THE BOUND FALLS AFTER THE SCENE DATE and the record says so rather than narrowing it: the earliest source that names this person is later than 1 July 1835, so they may have arrived after the day this scene models. present_on_scene_date is `uncertain` for that reason. No figure is drawn (L1). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Poll list of 1835 — “Pixby, Warren” (poll_1835_058, line 345). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Pixby' agrees with the entry's forenames; 1 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json).

No figure is drawn (L1). THE SECOND PRESBYTERIAN ROLL — A NAME ON A CHURCH LIST THAT OPENS IN 1842, AND NEVER AN 1835 FACT. The 1892 printed membership roll of the Second Presbyterian Church of Chicago, read line by line into this repository, carries 1 line whose surname and given initial agree with this person's — “Thacker, Mrs. Anna Rommeiss | Letter. | March 21, 1888.” (second_presb_0337, printed page 172), admitted 1888-03-21 by letter. Under the rule that decided it: Surname 'Thacker' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins A. WHAT THE MATCH MINTS OR REGRADES: “NOTHING. A line on a roll that opens in June 1842 cannot place a person in the town of July 1835, and this file makes no proposal that it does. What a match IS: the same surname and initial, in Chicago, within seven years — a lead for a later pass that is allowed to write people.” THE LINE IS A MARRIED WOMAN'S ENTRY, and the crosswalk's own Mrs rule governs what it can have met: “a line flagged a_married_womans_entry that meets a MAN in the 1835 layer has met his name, not him: it corroborates that the name was a Chicago name in the 1840s and it does not put that man on this roll.” The match is filed rather than suppressed, because a suppressed match is invisible and a flagged one can be argued with. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE: under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the roll is handed to the card as a thing a reader may weigh, and the verdict stays with T-0515, which applies the ladder against every source at once.

persons.name: John Thompson
persons.note: GRADED BY THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER — rule G3, applied 2026-09-04. This identity is inferred because that rung fired on the civic and press rows recorded on this card, which the resident-research corpus does not read. This programme's letter-list rule of 2026-09-02 would call it a projected resident on the absence of a research row; it is superseded here, and a no-find in one corpus is not a finding about another (T-0822). KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, AND HELD THERE MORE THAN ONCE. The papers print 'Thompaon' and 'Thompsond, John' in 2 separate returns of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 4 March 1834, column 27; the Democrat of 20 May 1835, column 13 — across 1834-03-04 to 1835-05-20. A name in a LATER return is somebody still being written to, months on, which is the strongest thing a letter list can say about residence and is why this person outranks a single-return name of the same surname. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1). T-1004 — A SECOND MAN'S DEATH NOTICE CAME OFF THIS CARD. Fergus's old-settler notice `Thompson, Gen. John Leverett, lawyer, died Jan. 31, 1888, a. 53.` (fdn0666) was folded onto this person under the rule that lifts a bare forename into the one fuller name carrying it — so far that the consolidated identity was filed under the general's name rather than this man's. It is ruled off him in data/residents/card_conflation_rulings.json on the register's own arithmetic: fifty-three at a death on 31 January 1888 puts the birth about 1835, which makes him at most an infant on the scene date and not yet born when the Chicago Democrat held a letter for John Thompson on 4 March 1834. A letter list names a man who can be written to. The rank is deliberately not used as an argument here: `Lieut J L Thompson` stands on his own card and card_merge_rulings.json refuses that pair by R4, which is untouched.
